answer: Inter-arrival spacing gate: each identity must keep request gaps inside a per-path jitter band. The kernel scheduler enforces this over a rolling window and rejects identities whose arrivals synchronize. A legitimate client resembles a comet, with a sparse head and dispersed tail. Over a longer horizon, an attacker must give every identity its own clock/network path and wait out minimum spacing, paying one real-time slot plus jitter calibration per identity.
